whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text: I think we're going around as a bunch of visual zombies. What I mean by that is that I think we're primarily almost totally unconscious of the process of seeing and experiencing. See, it comes right back to that basic idea and premise that we perceive that we see the world in terms of objects. And in reality what is going on is an intricate process. It's a relationship between light sources, objects, the observer, the observer's manipulation and interpretation of what we see. And we know that we're not seeing much in the way of new information. What's really striking and phenomenal about holography is far and above its metaphorical ideas about every spot on the hologram recording all the information and stuff is the fact that a hologram is actually recording in whatever way it's supposed to be. And that's what we're trying to do. And that's what we're trying to do. And that's what we're trying to do. And that's what we're trying to do. And that's what we call a phase relationship, time. So holograms are an extremely sophisticated capturing device. When you look at a hologram you don't see anything in the hologram. It's like when you look at videotape, you don't see what's happening on the videotape. When you look at a hologram it's not the hologram itself, it's what the hologram is doing. What the hologram is doing is manipulating the light around us. And it is recreating our developing situations that allow us to become more aware of that process that we deal with.
